ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the horizontal axis in the figure is labeled with locations 1—7, the right vertical axis is pressure (hPa), and the left vertical axis is longitude (E). The legend shows a longitude curve and a pressure curve. Location 6 is on the right side of the horizontal axis, corresponding to a longitude of about 120°E; near location 6, the pressure curve shows that the pressure on its west side is lower and the pressure on its east side is higher. Then reason: the stem states that all these locations are located at 31°N, belonging to the Northern Hemisphere. The pressure gradient force points from the high pressure on the east side toward the low pressure on the west side; in the Northern Hemisphere, air movement is deflected to the right by the geostrophic deflection force, and is affected by near-surface friction, so the actual wind direction is roughly from southeast to northwest. Wind direction is named according to the direction it comes from, so the main prevailing wind direction in the area where 6 is located is southeast wind.

raw_record.question_text:
The following figure is a “pressure distribution map of locations 1~77 on the 31°N latitude line in a certain month.” Read the figure and complete the small question.

<image1>

At this time, what is the main prevailing wind direction in the area where 6 is located?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify site 6 on the x-axis and note that longitude there is around 120°E, while the pressure curve has lower pressure to the west and higher pressure to the east. Then combine this with the text statement that all sites are on 31°N, i.e., in the Northern Hemisphere. Apply the pressure-gradient plus right-deflection rule: air on the west side of the eastern high-pressure area flows toward the lower pressure to the west/northwest after Coriolis/friction adjustment, so the wind comes from the southeast. Answer: 东南风.
